title: The Chapel at Midnight
summary: A clique in the goth scene is preparing a rite in one of the city's old chapels. Work out where and when, read which goths can be trusted, win the Sisters of Mercy over one by one and assemble a vigil before the countdown runs out.
timeRule: Time only moves when the player starts another day. Every reference is relative: 'tomorrow', 'in three days'. No weekdays, dates or clock times.

old_mission.name: the Old Mission Chapel
old_mission.phrase: where the bell forgot its voice
old_mission.lore: The Old Mission's bell cracked long ago and has not rung since.

cemetery_chapel.name: the Cemetery Chapel of Rest
cemetery_chapel.phrase: where the angels turn their backs on the city
cemetery_chapel.lore: At the Cemetery Chapel of Rest the stone angels face the desert, with their backs to the city.

st_brigid.name: St Brigid's Chapel
st_brigid.lore: St Brigid's keeps a copy of the saint's cloak above the altar.

lantern_vault.name: the Lantern Vault under the old viaduct
lantern_vault.lore: The Lantern Vault is the basement venue hosting the Midnight Show.

diaryPhrase: Not the show. When the moon closes her eye.

victoria.opening: I saw you looking at my flyer. ☾ You should come to the show. Come alone.
victoria.warning: ☾ I know which door is yours.

show.label: Ask about the Midnight Show
show.player: What actually happens at your show?
show.reply: Music. Then something older than music. Come alone. Bring nothing holy. ☾

crescent.label: Ask what the crescent means
crescent.player: What does the crescent on your flyer mean?
crescent.reply: It means a door is opening. Why is a little lamb asking?

accept.label: Say you'll come to the after-party
accept.player: I'll come to the after-party. Alone.
accept.reply: Good. I'll find you when it starts.

backout.label: Back out of Victoria's invitation
backout.reply: Nobody backs out of my invitations. I'll remember you.

confront.label: Tell her you know what she's planning
confront.player: I know what you're planning in that chapel. Call it off.
confront.reply: Then you know too much to keep. Sleep well.

MATCH-061.contactPlayer: Hi, I saw your name on the Midnight Show flyer.
MATCH-061.contactReply: Ha, that's me, early set. Two hours of records nobody's heard of. What's up?

MATCH-062.contactPlayer: Hi, the flyer says tickets come from you?
MATCH-062.contactReply: Yep, from the shop. Last few left. Buying, or just curious about the flyer?

MATCH-063.contactPlayer: Hi, did you draw the crescent on the Midnight Show flyer?
MATCH-063.contactReply: Took me all night. People keep staring at it. Like you, apparently.

show.label: Ask about the Midnight Show
show.player: So what's the Midnight Show actually like?

crescent.label: Ask what the crescent mark means
crescent.player: What does the crescent on the flyer mean?

help.label: Ask her to help you stop it
help.player: I think something bad is planned after the show. Will you help me stop it?

warn.label: Warn her to skip the after-party
warn.player: Do me a favour and skip the after-party. Please.

tell.label: Tell her the Sisters are planning a vigil
tell.player: The Sisters of Mercy are planning a vigil against whatever this is.

accuse.label: Accuse her of being part of it
accuse.player: I know you're part of whatever Victoria is planning.

innocent.show: Honestly it's just a gig. Bad lighting, good records, sticky floor. People get weird about the after-party, but I never stay for it.
innocent.crescent: It's the logo this month, it's on everything. Victoria wrote something odd in the booking diary though: 'Not the show. When the moon closes her eye.' Dramatic, right?
innocent.help: Stop what? You're starting to scare me. I just play records.
innocent.warn: Weird thing to say to someone you've never met. But fine. I wasn't staying anyway.
innocent.tell: Nuns with candles? That's adorable. I'm telling the group chat.
innocent.accuse: Are you serious? I'm telling everyone what a creep you are. Don't message me again.

sympathetic.show: It's... a gig. Mostly. Can we not talk about the after-party on here?
sympathetic.crescent: Please don't ask about that. Not on here.
sympathetic.help: Okay. I want out. It isn't at the show. It's afterwards, {phrase}. And not on the show night either: when the moon closes her eye. If anything changes, I'll tell you.
sympathetic.warn: You know, don't you. Thank you. I'll try to stay away.
sympathetic.tell: If the Sisters are really doing that, I'll stand with them. Somebody from our side should.
sympathetic.accuse: I can't do this. I can't. Don't message me again.

dangerous.show: It's more than a show. The after-party's at the Lantern Vault, everyone knows that. Come and see for yourself.
dangerous.crescent: Who told you to ask about that?
dangerous.help: Stop it? Oh, sweetheart. I'll pass that along.
dangerous.warn: Skip it? I'm working the door.
dangerous.tell: A vigil? How sweet. Which chapel?
dangerous.accuse: You've just made a very big mistake.

allyWarning: She's moved it. Victoria won't wait for the dark moon now. It's in {n} days.
allyWarningTomorrow: She's moved it. Victoria won't wait for the dark moon now. It's tomorrow.

chapelCall.label: Ask about crescent marks on chapel doors
chapelCall.reply: Yes, the Sisters have seen those marks. Margaret Holloway coordinates our volunteers. I'll pass on your name and she'll message you.
chapelCall.clue: St Brigid's passed your name to Margaret Holloway and the Sisters of Mercy.

MATCH-055.role: Organiser. Persuades the others to join.
MATCH-055.values: Order, responsibility and people who follow through.
MATCH-055.conditions: Show her real deciphered evidence and keep your word.
MATCH-055.intro: The office said you rang about crescent marks on chapel doors. I'm Margaret Holloway. I coordinate the parish volunteers. Before I take this seriously, tell me why you care.

topics.label: Say you want to help, whatever it costs
topics.player: I just want to help. Whatever it costs.
topics.reply: Plenty of people want to help until it costs them something. We'll see.

topics.label: Say it's the most exciting thing all year
topics.player: Honestly? This is the most exciting thing that's happened all year.
topics.reply: This is not entertainment. People's safety is not your hobby.

topics.label: Show her what you have deciphered
topics.player: Here's what I've worked out so far.

full.reply: Where and when. That's careful work. All right. I'm listening.

half.reply: Half an answer. Come back when you know where and when.

none.reply: Come back when you have more than a feeling.

topics.label: Ask whether she knows the old vigil prayers
topics.player: Do you know the old vigil prayers?
topics.reply: Some of them. Enough to lead on a quiet night, if three of us stand together. If they know we're coming, we'll need Teresa, who knows the whole office, and at least five voices.

topics.label: Ask who could hold the chapel door
topics.player: If they come to the chapel, who could hold the door?
topics.reply: Me, if it comes to that. I've stared down a bishop. I can stare down a girl in eyeliner. Evelyn would do too.

favour.offerLabel: Offer to help with the parish rota
favour.offerPlayer: Is there anything I can do for the parish?
favour.offerReply: Tomorrow I need someone to carry the vigil candles to the care home. Can I count on you?
favour.doLabel: Carry the candles to the care home
favour.doPlayer: Candles delivered to the care home, as promised.
favour.doReply: You came on the day you said you would. That matters to me.
favour.brokenReply: You said you would carry the candles. I carried them myself.

recruit.label: Ask her to organise a vigil
recruit.player: Will you organise a vigil with me?
recruit.yes: Then we do it properly. I'll talk to the others. They listen to me.
recruit.no: Not yet. I need to know you'll follow through.

after.success: We sang until the candles burned down. Thank you for not giving up on us.
after.failure: We were not where we needed to be. I keep thinking about it.

MATCH-056.role: Knows the old counter-prayer, the Watch of Mercy.
MATCH-056.doubts: Worries that you are mocking her faith.
MATCH-056.conditions: Be honest with her and never treat this as a joke.
MATCH-056.intro: Margaret says you've been asking about the old chapels. I teach history to ten-year-olds, so I warn you: I will over-explain.

topics.label: Ask about the city's old chapels
topics.player: What can you tell me about the city's old chapels?
topics.reply: There are three. The Old Mission's bell cracked long ago and has not rung since. At the Cemetery Chapel of Rest the stone angels face the desert, with their backs to the city. And St Brigid's keeps a copy of the saint's cloak above the altar.

topics.label: Ask if there's a prayer against something like this
topics.player: Is there a prayer against something like this?
topics.reply: There is an old office called the Watch of Mercy, sung through the night by candlelight. Very few people still know it. I do.

topics.label: Admit you're frightened
topics.reply: Good. Fear is honest. We can work with honest.

topics.label: Ask if she really believes in all this
topics.player: Do you really believe in all this stuff?
topics.reply: I believe in it enough to be offended. Goodnight.

topics.label: Ask if she could hold the door
topics.player: Could you hold the chapel door if they come?
topics.reply: Me? I'd faint. Put me at the altar with a book and I'm brave. Put me at a door and I'm useless.

topics.label: Ask what she makes of the goth crowd
topics.player: What do you make of the goth crowd?
topics.reply: Most of them are harmless. I've known {innocent} since school. Loud, never wicked. The others I don't know.

recruit.label: Ask her to lead the prayer at a vigil
recruit.player: Would you lead the Watch of Mercy at a vigil?
recruit.yes: I'll bring the book. And candles. So many candles.
recruit.no: I need to know you're not making fun of us first.

MATCH-056.accusedFriend: You accused {innocent}? She rang me in tears. She has never hurt anyone.

after.success: I've never sung the whole office through before. I don't think I'll ever forget it.
after.failure: I keep reading the office over and over, wondering what I got wrong.

MATCH-007.role: Carries the parish keys to every chapel.
MATCH-007.doubts: Afraid that an unsanctioned vigil will give the bishop an excuse to close the Sisters down.
MATCH-007.conditions: Show up for her with practical help and take her fear seriously.
MATCH-007.intro: Hello! Margaret mentioned you. I'm Sophia, I do the outreach rounds. Is everything all right?

topics.label: Ask who looks after the old chapels
topics.player: Who looks after the old chapels?
topics.reply: Our outreach group does. I carry the whole ring: the Mission, the Cemetery Chapel and St Brigid's. My handbag weighs a tonne.

topics.label: Ask how the bishop's review is affecting her
topics.player: How is the bishop's review affecting you?
topics.reply: If the bishop hears we held a vigil without permission, it could be the excuse he needs to shut us down. I'm frightened of that.

topics.label: Ask if she'd stand guard at the door
topics.player: Would you stand guard at the door?
topics.reply: I'd let anyone in who said please. That's rather my problem.

favour.offerLabel: Offer to help at the food pantry
favour.offerPlayer: Can I help at the pantry?
favour.offerReply: Would you? Tomorrow we're short of hands. Come and sort tins with me?
favour.doLabel: Sort tins at the pantry with Sophia
favour.doPlayer: I'm at the pantry. Where do the tins go?
favour.doReply: You came! The pantry has never been so organised. Thank you.
favour.brokenReply: We missed you at the pantry. I suppose something came up.

recruit.label: Ask her to bring the keys to a vigil
recruit.player: Would you bring the keys to a vigil?
recruit.yes: I'll bring the keys. All of them, just in case.
recruit.no: I want to help, I really do. I'm just scared. Give me a little time?

after.success: The bishop can say what he likes. We did the right thing.
after.failure: I locked up afterwards and my hands wouldn't stop shaking.

MATCH-057.role: Brings two steady volunteers from the parish council and can hold a door.
MATCH-057.doubts: Thinks provoking the goths will get somebody hurt.
MATCH-057.conditions: Promise not to tell any of the goth crowd about the Sisters, and keep that promise.
MATCH-057.intro: Evelyn Rosales. I keep the parish accounts. Margaret forwarded your name. I'll be honest: I think poking at those girls will get somebody hurt.

topics.label: Ask why she's so wary
topics.player: Why are you so wary of all this?
topics.reply: Because I've seen what happens when people poke at things they don't understand. Somebody always gets hurt, and it's never the one who poked.

topics.label: Promise not to tell the goth crowd about the Sisters
topics.player: I promise I won't tell any of the goth crowd about the Sisters.
topics.reply: Then I'll hold you to that. Small city. I'll know.

topics.label: Ask how many people she could bring
topics.player: How many people could you bring?
topics.reply: If I'm in, I bring two from the parish council. Steady people. And I'll hold a door against anyone.

topics.label: Tell her the goths are planning a murder
topics.player: They're planning a murder. I'm sure of it.
topics.reply: If you're going to frighten me with stories, do it somewhere else.

favour.offerLabel: Offer to help count the charity tins
favour.offerPlayer: Could you use help counting the charity tins?
favour.offerReply: Tomorrow, then. Bring a calculator and patience.
favour.doReply: You turned up and you can count. Rare qualities.
favour.brokenReply: You didn't come. I counted them alone. Noted.

recruit.label: Ask her to stand with the vigil
recruit.player: Will you stand with us at the vigil?
recruit.yes: Fine. I'm in. I'll bring two from the council.
recruit.no: No. Not until I trust you.

MATCH-057.promiseBroken: You told one of them about us. I said I'd know. Don't count on me.

after.success: Nobody got hurt. That's all I ever wanted.
after.failure: This is what I was afraid of.

messages.earlyVigil: Nothing came. We kept watch all night in the cold, and nothing came.
messages.refuseVigils: We've stood in the cold twice now. The Sisters won't gather again.
messages.markWarningClue: A silver crescent pendant was left outside your door. The coven knows who you are.
messages.allyAfterSuccess: It's over. She's gone quiet. Thank you for listening to me.
messages.innocentMissing: {innocent} hasn't answered anyone since the night of the rite.

show.title: MIDNIGHT SHOW FLYERS APPEAR ACROSS THE OLD QUARTER
show.summary: A basement gig under the old viaduct promises one night only, in three days.
show.body: The flyers carry a hand-drawn crescent and credits for DJ Alice Wren, tickets from Piper Nocturne at the Black Lace shop and artwork by Zara Brooks. The host signs only as V.B. In the margin of one flyer someone has added, in silver ink: 'Afterwards, {phrase}.'
show.clue: Midnight Show flyer, silver ink in the margin: 'Afterwards, {phrase}.'

skywatch.title: STORM CLEARS FOR THE DARKEST NIGHT OF THE SEASON
skywatch.summary: Forecasters say the sky will be moonless in {n} days.
skywatch.body: Once the dry storm front passes, the moon will thin to nothing. Stargazers are planning trips into the desert for the moonless night, due in {n} days.
skywatch.clue: Weather page: the moon disappears completely in {n} days (counted from day {day}).

heritage.title: SURVEY RECORDS THE CITY'S THREE OLD CHAPELS
heritage.summary: A cracked bell, stone angels and a famous cloak make the heritage list.
heritage.body: Volunteers have catalogued the city's three oldest chapels. The Old Mission's bell cracked long ago and has not rung since. The stone angels at the Cemetery Chapel of Rest face the desert, with their backs to the city. St Brigid's keeps a copy of the saint's cloak above its altar.
heritage.clue: Heritage survey: the Old Mission has the cracked bell, the Cemetery Chapel has the angels facing away from the city, St Brigid's has the cloak.

aftershow.title: LATE SHOW ENDS QUIETLY, BUT CHALK MARKS APPEAR
aftershow.summary: Crowds left the Lantern Vault peacefully. Two chapel doors were marked overnight.
aftershow.body: Neighbours say the Midnight Show ended without trouble. By morning, chalk crescents had appeared on the doors of {chalkA} and {chalkB}. Parish volunteers scrubbed them off.
aftershow.clue: After the show, chalk crescents appeared on {chalkA} and {chalkB}.

success.title: SISTERS' VIGIL ENDS A NIGHT OF DISTURBANCES AT {PLACE}
success.summary: Neighbours describe candles, singing and a group in black leaving quietly.
success.body: A vigil at {place} lasted through the night. Police say nobody was hurt. One neighbour said the air 'felt lighter' by morning.

success.title: LANTERN VAULT CLOSES ITS DOORS
success.summary: The basement venue under the viaduct has gone dark.
success.body: The organiser known as V.B. has not been seen since the vigil. Regulars say the crescent flyers have been torn down.

reconciled.title: UNLIKELY ALLIES SHARE A CANDLELIT VIGIL
reconciled.summary: Chapel volunteers and nightlife regulars stood together at {place}.
reconciled.body: Parish volunteers were joined by {sympathetic}, a regular at the Lantern Vault. 'Somebody from our side had to,' she said. Nobody was hurt.

reconciled.title: LANTERN VAULT CLOSES ITS DOORS
reconciled.summary: The basement venue under the viaduct has gone dark.
reconciled.body: The organiser known as V.B. has not been seen since the vigil. Regulars say the crescent flyers have been torn down.

partial.title: LIGHTS FAIL ACROSS OLD QUARTER DURING CHAPEL VIGIL
partial.summary: A vigil at {place} ended in darkness and conflicting accounts.
partial.body: Power failed for several streets while a small vigil prayed at {place}. Some witnesses describe a red glow, others nothing at all. The rite, if there was one, was not finished.

partial.title: QUESTIONS REMAIN AFTER NIGHT AT {PLACE}
partial.summary: The host of the Midnight Show has vanished.
partial.body: Nobody has seen the organiser known as V.B. since the blackout. A chalk crescent keeps reappearing on the chapel door, however often it is scrubbed away.

completed.title: STRANGE LIGHTS REPORTED NEAR {PLACE}
completed.summary: Residents describe a red glow and chanting.
completed.body: By the time police arrived, {place} was empty and its door was scorched with a crescent.{vigilNote}

completed.title: CONCERT-GOER MISSING AFTER NIGHT IN THE OLD QUARTER
CHAPEL CLOSED AFTER VANDALISM; PARISH 'SHAKEN'
completed.body: Detectives describe the scene as 'deeply unpleasant' but will not say more. The Sisters of Mercy declined to comment.

outcomes.missingInnocent: Friends of {innocent} say she has not answered her phone since the night of the rite. Her car was found on the desert road.
outcomes.missingStranger: Police are searching for a young man last seen near {place}. Friends say he 'followed the crowd' after the show.
outcomes.vigilElsewhere: Across town, a small vigil had gathered at {vigilPlace}.

outcomes.vigil_success: The vigil held. The Watch of Mercy was sung through the night at {place} and the rite was never finished.
outcomes.vigil_reconciled: The vigil held, and {sympathetic} stood with the Sisters. The rite was never finished, and some of the goth crowd turned away from it.
outcomes.vigil_partial: The vigil was too thin. The lights failed and the rite stalled, but it was not stopped. Victoria has vanished, and the mystery is unresolved.
outcomes.vigil_failed: The vigil at {place} fell apart. The prayer had no shape and the Sisters scattered. The rite was completed.
outcomes.wrong_place: The Sisters kept watch at {vigilPlace}, but the rite was at {place}. It was completed.
outcomes.too_late: The rite was completed at {place} before your vigil was due.
outcomes.ignored: Nobody stood against it. The rite was completed at {place}.
outcomes.withdrawn: You walked away. The rite was completed at {place}.

death.warningCaption: A crescent pendant lies in the hallway…

reasons.confront: You told Victoria you knew. She came through your door the next night.
reasons.marked_twice: The coven marked your door twice. Victoria came to collect.
reasons.ritual_marked: The rite was completed at {place}. Victoria remembered who tried to stop it.
reasons.watch_broken: Nobody held the chapel door. Victoria walked in, saw your face and followed you home.
reasons.went_alone: You went to Victoria's after-party alone.
